turns.reply:
This is a new system, so following CLAUDE.md I haven't written any code yet. I have questions first. The only thing pushed so far is the AI-use log, in PR https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/51. Plan usage: 5-hour 2%, weekly 20%.

From what's in the repo: the maze already has a bot in `src/systems/arcade/bot.js`. The cabinet runs that same maze game. The 7 deep layers are pure modules with a shared shape (`goal`, `update` returns dot/objective/hit), so one headless runner in Node can drive all of them.

**Questions (each has a suggested default):**

1. **Which layers get a bot?** Default: the maze and all 7 deep layers. The cabinet is skipped because it's the same game as the maze. The hall is skipped too unless it has a clear win condition.
2. **What counts as solved, and what counts as a loss?** Default: the maze is solved when level 1 is cleared before lives run out. A deep layer is solved when all its goals are done within a time cap (say 3 minutes of game time, to match "a run lasts 1 to 3 minutes"). Hits are recorded too.
3. **How strong should the bot be?** Default: a competent planner per layer that reads the same state the player sees (shortest path, avoiding the layer's enemy, keeping to its timing rules like "only while lit"). Human error then comes only from the noise, not from a deliberately weak bot.
4. **What kind of noise?** Default: three knobs that model a thumb on a phone:
   - reaction delay (0 to 400 ms)
   - swipe errors (0 to 30%: a swipe gets dropped or goes the wrong way)
   - late turns or overshoot (a turn lands one tile late)

   A single "skill" slider from 0 to 1 scales all three together. Each knob can also be swept on its own.
5. **How big a run?** Default: 5 noise levels × 20 seeded runs per layer, plus a `--quick` mode with 5 runs. Same seed means same result, so a balance change shows up as a real difference.
6. **Where does it live, and how do you see results?** Default: `tools/playtest.mjs` (Node, no build) writes a JSON report. A lab page `/lab/playtest.html` charts win rate against noise and time to solve for each layer. Optionally, the lab can also replay one run so you can watch it.
7. **What are we balancing toward?** Default proposal:
   - with no noise, every layer is won 100% of the time in 30 to 90 s
   - at medium noise, about 70% are won
   - difficulty rises as you go deeper

   I'd suggest config changes and you approve them before I make any.
8. **Should results be committed?** Default: commit a baseline report (e.g. `design/playtest/baseline.json`), refreshed whenever balance changes. No GitHub Actions run, to save time.

Answer "defaults" for any you don't care about.

**Cost:** writing 8 bots and the sweep is token-heavy, roughly one large session, while the runs themselves are free (local Node).

turns.reply:
The playtest framework is built, checked in, and has run the full sweep. It's in PR https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/51, and the results are charted at `/lab/playtest.html`. I took your missing answers as my suggested defaults.

**What it does**
- A bot plays each layer headless in Node on the real game code: the maze (swipes), the cabinet (joystick), the hall (collect coins, and the chase), and all 7 deep layers.
- **Full playthrough** mode runs the whole outer loop: the starting coin, game over, out of coins → up to the hall to collect coins → play on in the cabinet, then down through all 7 deep layers. If the input layer ends in game over, the bot goes back up for a coin. Moving between layers and tapping away text boxes count as time.
- **Noise:** late swipes (up to about 0.45 s at the top level), dropped swipes, swipes 90° off, and moments of not paying attention. Levels run from 0 (the bare bot) to 1 (sloppy). `--knob` sweeps one kind of noise alone.
- **Rerun:** `node tools/playtest.mjs` (20 runs per level, about 35 min of computer time, no tokens) or `--quick`. Results are written to `lab/playtest/results.json`.

**Results (win rate at noise 0 / 0.5 / 1)**

| Layer | Wins | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Maze / cabinet | 100% / 0% / 0% | The bot clears it every time with no delay, but loses almost every game once its reaction time passes about 0.2 s. |
| Bus | 0% at every level | Each door opens only when its chip is used. Reading a chip sends a packet out through the one-tile path to its door, so you can't get in. Only writes let you in, and video RAM gets about 1% of them; ROM never does. |
| Screen, video board, video RAM | 100% / 100% / 0–45% | A reasonable difficulty curve. |
| Input wires | 60% / 45% / 0% | The bot sometimes loses even with no noise, partly because the machine's Pac-Man game-overs. |
| CPU, logic | 85–100% everywhere | Probably too easy. |
| Hall | Coins easy; chase 100% / 15% / 0% | |
| Full playthrough | 0% | With no noise it always stops at the bus. From 0.5 up, it can't clear the maze with the 6 coins there are (1 to start, 5 in the hall). |

**How far to trust this:** the bots are only an estimate of a player. The maze bot in particular is a reactive planner, so a real person may do better there. The noise levels aren't yet tied to real players; the next human playtest should tell us which level matches you and Max.

I haven't changed any balance. Two candidates: let the bus doors open on reads too (or give the read packets a way around), and either slow the maze ghosts or give more coins.

Please open `/lab/playtest.html` on your phone and check the charts read well at phone width.
